acceptance: T033: write the test first (tests/test_api/): an edit-level person PATCHes visibility on a private dataset and on a private project: 403, stored visibility unchanged. A manager's PATCH still answers 200. An edit-level PATCH of another field (name) still answers 200. Smallest fix: one check on the update path (BaseViewSet.perform_update or the serializer's update) that refuses when a manager-only field (visibility, and the parent fields project, dataset, sample where the model has them) is in validated_data with a value different from the instance's and the requester cannot manage the record (RecordAccess(instance).can_manage). Reuse the names ManagerOnlyFieldsMixin (fairdm/core/forms.py) already holds rather than a second list, if it has one.

T034: test first, with a sample serializer that carries dataset (the default field list; see how the finding built it): an edit-level person PATCHes dataset to one they manage: 403, parent unchanged, their level unchanged. A manager moving the record to a parent that would leave it without a manager: 400, not 500 and not 200 (call RecordAccess(instance).refuse_move_without_manager for the changed parent before saving and turn its ValidationError into DRF's). A manager's valid move: 200. Same for a measurement.

T035: test first: a signed-in account with no credit POSTs a sample (and a measurement) into another team's public dataset: 400 (the dataset is not among the choices), nothing created, no contribution. A person at edit on the dataset: 201 and listed at manage. A person at view only: 400. Fix as the finding says: in the base sample and measurement serializers give the dataset field the choices the forms use (Dataset.all_objects.accessible_to(user, ContributionLevel.EDIT)), and do the same for a dataset's project field and a measurement's sample field where the serializer carries one. Anonymous stays 401.

T036: test first: for a private project, GET of the dataset list tab and the export tab answers 404 to a visitor and to a signed-in person with no credit, and 200 to a person at view. Fix as the finding says (PrivateRecordNotFoundMixin first in the bases and check = staticmethod(project_is_visible), as Overview does). Then look at every other plugin registered on Project, Dataset, Sample and Measurement in fairdm/ for the same gap and close any you find the same way, with a test each; name them in your report. SEC-005 (the sample editing pages answer 302/403 instead of 404) is LOW and out of scope: leave it.

T037: test first: a person at view on a project is not offered it on the dataset create form, and a POST naming it is refused; a person at edit is offered it. The dataset update form's project field offers the same set (still manage-only to change). Fix: Project's accessible_to(user, ContributionLevel.EDIT) in fairdm/core/dataset/forms.py, as the sample and measurement forms do for datasets.

T038: test first (page test through the client, in test_plugins/test_shared.py beside the edit tests): person at EDIT on the project and VIEW on the dataset; a manager POSTs the dataset's edit page with the preselected level (2) and a role change only: the dataset contribution's level is still VIEW and the roles changed. Posting level 3 stores MANAGE. Fix as the finding says: in ContributionEdit.post, when the posted level equals entry['above'] and is higher than entry['own'], pass level=None to Crediting.update. Do not touch the template.

T039: test first: the Contributors tab for a manager issues the same number of queries with 5 other people as with 25 (assert equality of the two counts, or a small fixed bound; not a hard-coded total). Fix as the finding says: fetch the real contributors once and the levels on the chain once in ContributionList.get_context_data and have describe() read from them. The edit and remove pages call describe() for one contribution: keep them working. Do not change what the page draws.

T040: docs/more/migration-guides.md: Dataset.all_objects.with_level(...) and one clause saying Dataset.objects leaves private datasets out. docs/portal-development/restful-api.md near line 102: after T033 to T035 the sentence that the API enforces the same object-level rules is true; add what a reader must know (visibility and the parent need manage; a record is created only inside a parent held at edit). docs/portal-development/contributors.md near line 1020: the ask signature as services/registries.py has it (keyword-only after parse). docs/portal-administration/managing_users_and_permissions.md: what reversing the upgrade does, as the migrations have it (read 0022 and 0023 and state only what is true).
